## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.24 — Say why the desktop build failed

> **Alpha.** Diagnostics only. If the Linux desktop build was failing for you,
> this build should tell you why instead of scrolling past it.

### The error pointed at the wrong layer

Electron explains its own failures on its own stderr — a missing X server, a
sandbox complaint, a missing library. That got relayed as an ordinary log line
somewhere in the middle of the output, and then the program exited saying
`open window: context canceled`, which describes nothing.

So the last thing on screen — the part anyone copies into a bug report — was
the symptom, and the cause was buried a hundred lines up. Electron's own words
are now attached to the error itself, under **"what Electron reported"**.

### Running without a desktop now says so

Over SSH, in a container, or on a headless machine you used to get a wall of
Chromium logging ending in a cancelled context. Now:

```
no graphical display: both DISPLAY and WAYLAND_DISPLAY are unset.
  This build opens a desktop window and needs one. Either:
    huemux-desktop --headless    same server, no window
    huemux                       the plain server binary
  and open the printed URL in a browser
```

### What this does not do

It does not fix a crash. I could not reproduce one: on a Linux box the plain
server runs, the headless desktop build runs, and under a virtual display the
desktop build opens its window and finishes loading. Whatever is happening is
specific to the machine it happens on.

If it still fails, the output from this build is the thing to send — along with
the first line it prints, which reports your session type and display
variables. Wayland is the most likely difference.
